limitations_and_items_before_freeze_or_b: Synthetic state association checks do not establish Atari identity accuracy, ME, semantic objects, learning, transfer or a gate result.

The caller must define a monotone observation clock and the horizon actually represented by the displacement. The module cannot attest paid-frame provenance, terminal/cold reset policy, branch-clock alignment or native restoration.

Every update deep-copies tracking memory and allocates a dense N_tracks by(N_instances+N_tracks) assignment matrix. There is currently no independent active/coasting track capacity. A4096-instance bound per image does not bound accumulated tracks to4096. A prospective capacity, explicit refusal behavior and measured cost are required before benchmark or collection.

Maximum-cardinality assignment prefers any geometrically admissible match over leaving a track unmatched, even with poor appearance. This is a disclosed candidate association rule, not a proof of identity.

Zero or near-zero mean embeddings contribute no distinguishing appearance evidence under the current cosine fallback. Constant-velocity coasting and appearance averaging remain unvalidated under occlusion, acceleration, splitting, merging and changing appearance.
The visual groups can themselves contain disconnected pieces or multiple same-appearance objects. Tracking them does not repair the limitations of P targets or establish physical objecthood.

Readonly input outputs are not a security boundary. Internal stored descriptors are copied, but TrackedObservation exposes the caller supplied VisualInstance; callers must not confuse this returned view with an immutable external audit record.
The numeric tolerance is declared from floating-point uncertainty; no empirical enlargement of the eight-pixel radius has been selected on game data.
The pending counterfactual C targets, collector, action/effect discovery and any native branch integration are explicitly outside this receipt and require separate review.
